How it is measured and what limits the result

This measures phone-to-server speed over the active connection: Wi-Fi, mobile data, ethernet or VPN. On a metered network (mobile data) a data estimate is shown before the test. The ceiling is the PHY link rate (in practice about 60–70 %), channel load, the router, the ISP line and the server uplink (rychlost.zelina.eu is a colleague's server on Proxmox, M-Lab is shared infrastructure). One test transfers hundreds of MB up to a few GB.

LibreSpeed: 6 parallel HTTPS downloads and 3 uploads of random data, 10 s per direction, the first 2–4 s of ramp-up are excluded. Latency is an HTTP request to empty.php over a kept-alive connection (median; jitter = mean difference of consecutive samples); it includes server processing and is not an ICMP ping.

NDT7: one WebSocket connection, the server ends the test within 10 s, the app after 15 s at most. It has no ping of its own; latency comes from the server's TCP_INFO (MinRTT and RTT during download). The server measures the whole test including ramp-up, the client excludes the first seconds, so a difference is expected; the server's upload figure is more accurate. Run both engines to compare.

History keeps the last 20 results on the phone only, excluded from backup. No IP address is stored.

The NDT7 test runs on Measurement Lab servers. M-Lab stores every test including the public IP address it came from and publishes it as open data (internet research). Anyone reading M-Lab data can see that IP address. If that is fine, continue; the app remembers your consent. Otherwise use LibreSpeed.
